page.layout: Top: two engraved medallion portraits with legends in their margins (left: R. ISRAEL / IEHV; right: IOIADA / SV SAC.). Below them: one block of running text in two paragraphs, with the text in one column. Below the text: a printed fleuron ornament, no text.

main_text.l: R. ISRAEL IEHV
SV SAC. IOIADA
IEHV, Dux exercitus Ioram, Regis Iudæ, imperante in
Israël Ioram filio Achab, & Ochosia filio alterius Ioram in Iu-
da vnctus est in Regem Israël, regnauitque his duobus inter-
fectis, anno mundi quo Athalia, de qua proxima pagina supe-
riore à nobis dictum est. Hic omnem domum Regis Achab ex-
terminauit: Ioram Regem Israël sagitta transfuerberauit. Ocho-
siam occidit, Iezabel præcipitari iussit. Consulito lib. 4. Reg. ca. 9.
& 10. & Iosep. lib. Antiq. 9. cap. 6. Hic sacerdotes Baal occidit,
idolum, & templum succendit, in quo loco cloacas fecit: nec
tamen à peccatis Ieroboam recessit, nec dereliquit vitulos au-
reos, qui erant in Bethel, & in Dan. imperauit annos 28. & suc-
cessit ei Ioachas filius eius.
IOIADA summum obtinuit apud Iudæos Sacerdotium:
hic Ioas Ochosiæ Regis Iudæ filium, in regnum restituit, occi-
sa Athalia, quæ tyrannide regnum invaserat. pepigit Ioiada fœ-
dus cum Ioas, quo fœdere Rex Ioas & ipse populus polliciti
sunt obedire Deo, & populus etiam Regi inito hoc fœdere,
demoliti sunt aras Baal, idola contriverunt. & Mathan sacerdo-
tem Baal, occiderunt, etiam coram altari. Vide li. 4. Reg. cap. 11.
nihilominus tamen mortuo Ioiada, Ioas ipse ad idololatriam
deflexit. Vide lib. 2. Paral. 24. cap. & Iosep. lib. Antiq. 9. cap. 7.

page.notes: Two engraved medallions with portraits; their legends are printed in the engraving and are given above as lines. Legend "SV SAC." is partly cut off by the medallion edge. Ochosiam in the text is set as "Ocho-fiam" across a line end; long s read as s. The printed "Ochô" at line end is read as Ocho. Medallion legends "IEHV" and "IOIADA" are set in capitals. Printed word errors left as printed: "Regi.inito" (no space), "sacerdo tem" (line-end split without hyphen, written whole), "nihilom nus" (written whole as nihilominus). Some punctuation in the citations ("Iosep.lib.Antiq.9.cap.6.") is printed without spaces.
